_note: Campfire smoke (docs/design/fire_smoke_wind_design.md; Dave 10 Nov 2026: 'its hovering around like flies. it should be drifting away with the breeze'). Each puff leaves the flames rising at rise_m_s for the fire's tier (small, medium, large) and moving with the world wind (weather_look.gd set_fire_air: speed and where it blows toward). It rises more slowly as it goes, down to rise_end_share of its start by the end of its life_s, and spreads (it grows grow_to times its start size, puff_m by tier) and fades. In near calm (wind under calm_mps[0], bending from there to calm_mps[1]) it goes straight up at calm_rise_m_s at least. On a still clear night it rises at night_rise_m_s and stops at about night_top_m, spreading flat. spread_deg is the cone the puffs leave in, [calm, windy]. No noise steers the puffs (the old turbulence turned each puff's velocity toward a random noise direction within a second, so the puffs wandered round the fire like flies).
_note_plume: Dave 10 Nov 2026 ('make fire smoke actually look and act more like fire smoke'): one continuous plume, not puffs. amount is many small overlapping puffs (each only alpha of the full density), starting puff_m wide and growing grow_to times (narrow at the fire, wide up high). Each puff is near_grey at the fire and far_grey by the end (dark and dense low, light and thin high); fade is the density over its life [[life share, density]...]. wind_start_share: a fresh puff rises on its heat with only this share of the wind, and the wind takes it fully by the end of its life, so the plume bends over more the higher it goes. waver_m: the column sways this far by the end of its life, the same at the same height (one wavering column, not jitter). coals: the thin wisp from a bed of glowing coals.
